title: Turkey Zoodle Bolognese
shortDescription: Lean turkey ragu over spiralized zucchini with parmesan
subtitle: Lean turkey ragu over spiralized zucchini with parmesan
description: Ground turkey simmers in tomato-wine bolognese while zucchini noodles stay separate for a lighter hall pasta alternative.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Turkey Zoodle Bolognese in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch turkey. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Salt and drain zoodles
steps.instruction: Toss spiralized zucchini with 1 tsp salt, rest 10 minutes in a colander. Squeeze out moisture with towels so noodles stay firm when sauced.

steps.title: Brown turkey
steps.instruction: Cook ground turkey in olive oil over medium-high 8–10 minutes, breaking into fine crumbles until no pink remains and edges look lightly golden.

steps.title: Build bolognese base
steps.instruction: Add onion, carrot, celery; cook 6 minutes. Add garlic, tomato paste, Italian seasoning; cook 2 minutes until paste darkens to brick red.

steps.title: Simmer sauce
steps.instruction: Add wine, reduce 3 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes, simmer 20 minutes uncovered until thick and spoon-coating with visible turkey throughout. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Turkey Zoodle Bolognese onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Sear zoodles and plate
steps.instruction: Sauté zoodles in hot oiled skillet 2–3 minutes until just warmed and slightly tender. Top with bolognese and parmesan at the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Turkey Zoodle Bolognese — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Do not sauce zoodles until plating—they turn soggy in holding pans.
A pinch of nutmeg in bolognese adds classic depth.
Regular spaghetti on the side keeps both camps happy.
tonightSpread: Garlic bread for crew who skip zoodles.
leftovers: Sauce over regular pasta next day—zoodles do not reheat well.
Freeze bolognese without zoodles for future pasta nights.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Comfort food flavor without carb coma. Crew gets protein-heavy sauce with fresh vegetable base.
mealPrepNotes: Spiralize zucchini day-of—pre-spiralized zoodles weep water. Salt and drain 10 minutes before cooking. Station: Cook zoodles in batches in hot skillet 2 minutes only—overcooking makes watery plates. Station: Keep sauce and zoodles separate until plating for best texture. Station: Offer regular pasta on the side for crew who want both options.
